landmarks.name: Baalbek
landmarks.writeup: Ancient Roman temple complex known for its grand architecture and historical significance.

wiki.extract: Baalbek is a city located east of the Litani River in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley, about 67 km (42 mi) northeast of Beirut. It is the capital of Baalbek-Hermel Governorate. In 1998, the city had a population of 82,608. Most of the population consists of Shia Muslims, followed by Sunni Muslims and Christians; in 2017, there was also a large presence of Syrian refugees.

landmarks.name: Jeita Grotto
landmarks.writeup: A system of interconnected limestone caves famous for its stunning stalactites and stalagmites.

wiki.extract: The Jeita Grotto is a system of two separate, but interconnected, karstic limestone caves spanning an overall length of nearly 9 kilometres (5.6 mi). The caves are situated in the Nahr al-Kalb river valley within the locality of Jeita, 18 kilometres (11 mi) north of the Lebanese capital Beirut. Though inhabited in prehistoric times, the lower cave was not rediscovered until 1836 by Reverend William Thomson; it can only be visited by boat since it channels an underground river that provides fresh drinking water to more than a million Lebanese.

landmarks.name: Byblos
landmarks.writeup: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, rich in archaeological sites.

wiki.extract: Byblos, also known as Jbail, Jebeil, Jbeil or Jubayl, is an ancient city in the Keserwan-Jbeil Governorate of Lebanon. The area is believed to have been first settled between 8800 and 7000 BC and continuously inhabited since 5000 BC. During its history, Byblos was part of numerous cultures including Canaanite, Egyptian, Phoenician, Assyrian, Persian, Hellenistic, Roman, Genoese, Mamluk and Ottoman. Urbanisation is thought to have begun during the third millennium BC when it developed into a city, making it one of the oldest cities in the world, if not the oldest. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

landmarks.name: Cedars of God
landmarks.writeup: Ancient cedar forest, symbolizing Lebanon and mentioned in various historical texts.

wiki.extract: The Cedars of God is a forest in the Kadisha Valley of Bsharre, Lebanon. It is a vestige of the extensive forests of the Lebanon cedar that thrived across Mount Lebanon in antiquity. Early modern travelers' accounts of the wild cedars appear to refer to the ones in Bsharri; the Christian monks of the monasteries in the Kadisha Valley venerated the trees for centuries. The earliest documented references of the Cedars of God are found in Tablets 4–6 of the Epic of Gilgamesh.

landmarks.name: Beirut National Museum
landmarks.writeup: Houses a vast collection of archaeological artifacts showcasing Lebanon's history.

wiki.extract: The National Museum of Beirut is the principal museum of archaeology in Lebanon. The collection begun after World War I, and the museum was officially opened in 1942. The museum has collections totaling about 100,000 objects, most of which are antiquities and medieval finds from excavations undertaken by the Directorate General of Antiquities.

cultural_events.name: Beirut International Film Festival
cultural_events.writeup: Annual event showcasing regional and international films, promoting cultural exchange.

wiki.extract: A growing number of film festivals are held in the Arab world to showcase films from the region as well as international standouts. In addition, institutions and organizations in other parts of the world are increasingly honoring the new generation of filmmakers in the Arab world with Arab film festivals.

cultural_events.name: Byblos International Festival
cultural_events.writeup: Music and arts festival held in the ancient city of Byblos featuring global artists.

wiki.extract: The Byblos International Festival is a Lebanese festival held in Byblos, believed to be the first Phoenician city, founded around 5000 BC. The festival is the biggest in Lebanon, and attracts thousands of tourists from all over the world.

cultural_events.name: Mawazine Festival
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrates Lebanese music and culture with performances across the country.

wiki.extract: Mawazine is an international music festival held annually in Rabat, Morocco. The event features a wide range of international and local music artists across various genres. Mawazine is organized by Maroc Cultures.

food_writeup: Lebanese cuisine is known for its use of fresh ingredients, olive oil, herbs, and spices, featuring dishes like hummus, tabbouleh, kibbeh, and manakish.
brief_history: Lebanon has a rich history dating back to ancient Phoenician civilization. It has been influenced by various empires including Roman, Ottoman, and French. Lebanon gained independence in 1943 and has experienced periods of conflict and cultural flourishing.
